entries.rationale: The deterministic normalization tier is useful, but the optional LLM fallback remains default-off until its incremental semantic-gap recovery and latency are measured on representative supported hardware.

exitCriteria.promoteWhen: A representative end-to-end evaluation shows semantic-gap recovery beyond the deterministic tier, no retrieval-quality regression, and p95 normalization latency within the search timeout on supported CPU and GPU tiers.
exitCriteria.removeWhen: The LLM fallback adds no material recovery beyond deterministic normalization, exceeds the supported-tier latency budget, or is superseded by a non-LLM normalization path.

entries.rationale: Soft-boost query understanding remains default-off until representative user-query incidence and supported-hardware preprocessing latency justify adding an automatic LLM stage to every eligible search.

exitCriteria.promoteWhen: Representative local-query evaluation demonstrates positive retrieval impact and p95 preprocessing latency within the search budget on supported CPU and GPU tiers, with no unresolved scheduling contention.
exitCriteria.removeWhen: Representative evaluation shows non-positive retrieval impact, unacceptable supported-tier latency, or explicit agent and user filters make the automatic preprocessing stage redundant.
